title: Strings
overview:
A string is a data structure used to store a sequence of characters such as letters, numbers, spaces, and symbols.

You can think of a string as a sequence where each character has a position called an index.

String:  H  E  L  L  O
Index:   0  1  2  3  4

Here, each character can be accessed using its index:

str[0] → H
str[2] → L
str[4] → O

In many programming languages, strings are internally represented using an array-like sequence of characters, which is why many string operations are similar to array operations.
whyUse:
Strings are used whenever we need to store and work with text or sequences of characters.

For example:

Name     → "Chandni"
Message  → "Hello World"
Password → "abc123"

Instead of storing every character separately, a string keeps the complete sequence together and allows us to process it as a single value.
howItWorks:
A string stores characters in a specific order, and each character has an index.

String:  C  O  D  E
Index:   0  1  2  3

If we want the character at index 2:

str[2]
  ↓
Access character at index 2
  ↓
D
This index-based access is similar to accessing an element in an array.
The exact way strings are stored and modified can differ between programming languages. Some languages treat strings as immutable, meaning their contents cannot be changed directly after creation.

operations.name: Access
operations.description:
Getting a character using its index.

str[1] → O

Typically O(1).

operations.name: Traversal
operations.description:
Visiting each character one by one.

For example, traversal can be used to count characters, check conditions, or process every character.

O(n).

operations.name: Concatenation
operations.description:
Joining two or more strings together.

"Hello" + "World"
        ↓
"HelloWorld"

operations.name: Comparison
operations.description:
Comparing two strings to check whether they are equal or determine their ordering.

"abc" == "abc" → true
"abc" == "abd" → false

Comparison may require checking characters one by one, so it can take O(n) in the worst case.

operations.name: Searching
operations.complexity: O(n) or more depending on the algorithm
operations.description:
Finding a character or a sequence of characters inside a string.

"datastructure"
     ↑
    "str"

String searching is commonly used to find characters or patterns.

operations.name: Modification
operations.description:
Creating a changed version of a string by replacing, inserting, or removing characters.

Before: "CAT"
Change: "C" → "B"
After:  "BAT"

The exact cost depends on the programming language and how strings are implemented.

complexity.time: Access character — O(1), Traversal — O(n), Comparison — O(n), Searching — O(n) or more depending on the algorithm
notes: Access is typically O(1) because a character can be accessed using its index.
Operations that examine characters one by one can take O(n).

keyTakeaways: A string stores a sequence of characters in a specific order.
Characters can usually be accessed directly using their index.
Common string operations include access, traversal, concatenation, comparison, searching, and modification.
String behavior and modification can differ between programming languages, especially because some languages use immutable strings.
Strings are widely used in DSA for text processing and pattern-based problems.
